title: EdgeGuard-Sentinel CDN, WAF & Origin IP Firewall Finding
summary: Audited CDN edge response headers and executed non-destructive micro-fuzzing loops on MacBook-Air.local. Detected 10 edge vulnerabilities. Intercepted deployment hook and applied WAF patch.
evidence: Wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin '*' permits arbitrary origin cross-domain requests
Direct Origin Routing Detected: Missing CDN proxy layer headers (cf-ray / x-amz-cf-id)
Backend Origin IP Leaked in header 'Server': 172.16.57.163
Backend Origin IP Leaked in header 'X-Backend-Server': 10.0.4.15
Backend Origin IP Leaked in response payload/WebRTC candidate: 192.168.1.100
Fuzzing endpoint https://staging-edge.kvch-hub.internal/api/v1 with Path Traversal Probe -> Endpoint returned 200 OK for /../../../../etc/passwd without WAF path sanitization
Fuzzing endpoint https://staging-edge.kvch-hub.internal/api/v1 with HTTP Request Smuggling Vector -> Edge proxy accepted ambiguous Transfer-Encoding + Content-Length headers
Fuzzing endpoint https://staging-edge.kvch-hub.internal/api/v1 with Custom Header Injection (X-Forwarded-Host) -> Host header override permitted without CDN host validation
recommended_actions: Inject Strict-Transport-Security, CSP, and X-Frame-Options headers on edge proxies
Obscure backend origin IPv4 addresses behind CDN reverse proxies
Enable EdgeGuard automated deployment hook locking on staging CI/CD pipelines
